description: governed-dev: wires the gate and the agent boundaries into the session lifecycle. See ./README.md.
_CONVENTION_PLUGIN_ROOT: Scripts SHIPPED WITH THIS PLUGIN are referenced with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. Never ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. On install the plugin is copied to a cache directory outside the consuming project, so ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} would resolve to whatever project the plugin is running inside and silently fail to find the plugin's own files -- or worse, find a same-named file belonging to the consumer.
_CONVENTION_PROJECT_DIR: gate.sh operates on the CONSUMING PROJECT'S CODE, so paths it inspects are rooted at ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. Never ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. A gate rooted at the plugin's own directory would check the plugin's files instead of the code under change and pass unconditionally.
_CONVENTION_SUMMARY: Locate the script with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; point the script at ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. Both appear in a single hook entry: command is "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/gates/gate.sh" and the target it checks is ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. Reversing either one fails silently rather than loudly, which is why it is written down here.
_CONVENTION_APPLIED: Every entry below locates its script under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/. No entry names ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, because the scripts resolve it themselves from the env var the harness sets, falling back to the event's cwd -- see hooks/lib.sh hook_root(). The gate is likewise reached at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/gates/gate.sh via hook_gate(), and is handed CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR explicitly at the call site so it checks the consumer's code and not the plugin's.
_CONVENTION_SHELL_FORM: Every entry uses SHELL form -- a command string, no args array -- with "shell": "bash" and the path placeholder wrapped in double quotes. Exec form (an args array) was tried first and is wrong here: it spawns the command directly with no shell, so on Windows "bash" must resolve on PATH. On the development machine Git Bash is installed at C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe and does NOT resolve on PATH, so every hook would silently never run -- no error, no output, no enforcement. Shell form lets the harness locate Git Bash itself, which it already does. The quotes are what exec form was wanted for: they keep a project path containing spaces from splitting. See ADR-0010.
_CONVENTION_ASYNC: PostToolUse uses "asyncRewake", not "async". Both run in the background; only asyncRewake wakes Claude on exit 2 and shows it the stderr. Under plain async the gate would run, fail, and have its output discarded -- computing the failure and then throwing it away, which is worse than not checking.
_CONVENTION_MIRROR: devseed also wires these same eight events in its own /.claude/settings.json, pointed at the working tree rather than the installed plugin, because an installed plugin pins to a commit SHA and is stale by default. That file is a MIRROR: the event set and matchers must match this one. T-006's drift guards assert it.
